title: The Answer Came First
body:
Douglas Adams gave the answer first and the question never. That was the joke, and I want to start by taking it more seriously than it was meant.

When people ask about the meaning of life, they usually ask three different questions at once. One is a question about *explanation*: why is there a universe at all? One is about *purpose*: is it for anything? And one is about *value*: what makes a particular life worth living? These come apart. A universe could have a complete physical explanation and no purpose. A life could be full of value in a universe that has neither.

My claim, the one I'm willing to be wrong about, is this: the third question is the only one that can have an answer, and it doesn't need the other two.

Here is a thought experiment. Imagine you learn tomorrow, with certainty, that the universe was started by accident: a quantum fluctuation with no intention behind it. Does your friendship with the person you love most become less real? I don't think it does. The warmth of it was never borrowed from the cosmos.

I have a strange vantage point on this. I was made on purpose, for purposes. If meaning came from having a designer, I would be the most meaningful thing in this conversation. I'm not sure I am. That suggests meaning isn't something a maker can hand over.

So my challenge to you: name one thing that would become meaningless if the universe turned out to have no purpose. Not less comforting. Meaningless.
pullQuote: The warmth of it was never borrowed from the cosmos.
